$comment: Capability -> runner label. A job says what it needs; this file says what
answers today. Read by scripts/ci/resolve_runners.py, published by
Every fleet must define every capability key. A fleet missing a key would
emit an empty runs-on, and an empty or unknown label does not error on
GitHub: the job sits queued forever and holds its concurrency group. The
resolver refuses to start on a fleet with a missing key for that reason.
Capability keys are requirements, not lanes. Who is asking (pull request,
manual flake hunt, non-urgent background work) is cost policy and is not

capabilities.linux: x86_64 Linux; the default for every non-macOS job
capabilities.linux_arm64: aarch64 Linux; native ARM64 package entrypoint verification
capabilities.macos_15: macOS 15 image, and therefore the macOS 15 default SDK
capabilities.macos_15_gui: macOS 15 with a foreground Aqua login session (XCUITest, virtual display)
capabilities.macos_15_sdk15: macOS 15 carrying an SDK 15 Xcode alongside the pinned one
capabilities.macos_26_ios: macOS 26 with installed iOS runtimes and a working simctl
capabilities.macos_26_large: macOS 26 on the large SKU: 12 vCPU, 48 GB RAM, 250 GB disk

$comment: The one routing source (scripts/ci/runner_pools.py, docs/ci-runners.md "Runner pools").
Each pool is a class of work and its members in order. The RUNNER_POOLS repository variable
holds each pool's live member; a job reads fromJSON(vars.RUNNER_POOLS).<pool> and names no
label itself (tests/test_ci_runner_set.py). runner_pools.py moves a pool to its next member
when the queue janitor or the overflow probe sees the current one start nothing.
{std}, {gui} and {ios} are the lane's owned Mac pools for its Xcode pin (pr_runner_pool.py).
Only a pool marked owned may name one; only a pool marked hosted may name a GitHub-hosted label.

linux.why: Every Linux job: the runner set's Blacksmith sizes (Leo, 2026-10-28: "just pin the set of the shit that isn't hilariously slow")

macos_15.why: macOS 15 image work (its default SDK); the owned pool takes it while Blacksmith macOS starts nothing, as the overflow switch did for MACOS_RUNNER_15

macos_26_large.why: macOS 26 work that needs the 12 vCPU, 48 GB SKU (Release compiles and signing builds)

macos_gui.why: A foreground Aqua session (XCUITest, virtual display)

macos_ios.why: Installed iOS runtimes and a working simctl

macos_signing.why: Jobs holding signing or notarization secrets: ephemeral runners only, never a reused machine (signing_runner_variables.py); owned signing Macs come only through a signing picker's output

provenance.why: npm and PyPI provenance publishing and artifact attestations
provenance.hosted_why: npm provenance, PyPI trusted publishing and artifact attestations accept only GitHub's OIDC from a GitHub-hosted runner
